review_notes: Read the whole file. Searched Mathlib for a categorical distribution (none by name) and for the PMF API: PMF.ofFintype, PMF.toMeasure, toMeasure_apply_singleton, toMeasure_map_apply, PMF.integral_eq_sum. Checked TauCeti for a StdSimplex↔PMF bridge (none found in Geometry/Convex) and for uses of categoricalMeasure (only this file). The multinomial measure is also built as a weighted Dirac sum, so the choice is consistent within the library. The Dirac-sum representation, the StdSimplex parameterisation, the one-hot/multinomial bridge and the measurability in the parameter are all deliberate, so I only flag the overlap with PMF as a moderate-confidence finding. I did not find other competing concepts. Uncertainty: whether the maintainers prefer a Measure-first API, and whether PMF-based lemmas would apply directly given the NNReal-to-ENNReal coercion.

findings.excerpt:
def categoricalMeasure (p : StdSimplex NNReal I) : Measure I :=
  ∑ i, (p.weights i : ENNReal) • Measure.dirac i
findings.problem: On a finite type, this is the measure of the finitely supported probability mass function `PMF.ofFintype (fun i => (p.weights i : ℝ≥0∞)) _`, taken through `PMF.toMeasure`. Mathlib already has that concept, with API for singleton masses (`PMF.toMeasure_apply_singleton`), pushforward (`PMF.toMeasure_map_apply`, `PMF.map`) and finite-sum integration (`PMF.integral_eq_sum`). The file does not define a bridge from `StdSimplex` to `PMF`, nor does any other TauCeti file I found. It re-proves the same three facts for its own measure: `categoricalMeasure_singleton`, `map_categoricalMeasure` and `integral_categoricalMeasure`. Because there is no bridge lemma, a user holding a `PMF` on a fintype cannot reuse these lemmas, and the PMF lemmas cannot be reused on categorical laws. Conversions must be proved ad hoc.
findings.proposed_change: Keep `categoricalMeasure` as the named StdSimplex-parameterised entry point, but connect it to Mathlib. One option is to add a lemma such as `categoricalMeasure p = (PMF.ofFintype (fun i => (p.weights i : ℝ≥0∞)) p.total_ENNReal).toMeasure`, with a short docstring saying it is the PMF measure. The other is to define `categoricalMeasure` as that `toMeasure`. Either way, derive the singleton, pushforward and integral lemmas from the existing PMF ones, or state them via the bridge, so future users can move between `StdSimplex`, `PMF` and `Measure`.
findings.benefit: Avoids a parallel finite-distribution API next to PMF. It lets categorical laws reuse the PMF lemmas, for example `PMF.integral_eq_sum` and `PMF.toMeasure_map_apply`. It also gives users an explicit conversion with PMF-based code, such as `PMF.bernoulli` and the PMF marginal files in TauCeti.

evidence.excerpt: def ofFintype [Fintype α] (f : α → ℝ≥0∞) (h : ∑ a, f a = 1) : PMF α :=
theorem toMeasure_apply_singleton (a : α) (h : MeasurableSet ({a} : Set α)) :
∫ a, f a ∂(p.toMeasure) = ∑ a, (p a).toReal • f a
∫ i, g i ∂categoricalMeasure p = ∑ i, (p.weights i : ℝ) • g i
